title: M-03 staked-subset notional S = totalStaked * latestPrice uses bare multiplication; safe for documented param envelope but unprotected against future high-supply / high-price configs
description: `_recomputeSchedule` computes the staked-subset notional as `S = totalStaked * latestPrice` with no overflow guard. NatSpec bounds the product at ~1e27 under current params, but `totalStaked` is not enforced on-chain and a future `stakedId` rotation to a higher-supply token combined with sustained `growthBasisPoints` mints can push the product past `2^256`.
impact: No exploitable loss today. If parameters drift outside the documented envelope (`totalStaked * latestPrice` approaching `2^256`), Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic reverts in `_recomputeSchedule`, DoS-ing every user-facing function except `emergencyWithdraw` (stake / unstake / claim / topUp / setTargetAPY / setDispatcherIndex / setNFTMinter / pullAndRefresh all revert). Solvency is preserved (principal recoverable via `emergencyWithdraw`).
attackPath: [Hypothetical] Owner reconfigures dispatcher to a higher-supply token ID + sustained mints push latestPrice into the high range
stake / unstake / claim / topUp / setTargetAPY / setDispatcherIndex / setNFTMinter / pullAndRefresh all revert
Stakers exit via emergencyWithdraw (forfeiting pending reward)
recommendation: Cheapest defensive hardening: `require(latestPrice == 0 || totalStaked <= type(uint256).max / latestPrice, NFTStaker__SOverflow())` before the bare mul, with a typed error so monitoring can react before total-interaction DoS sets in. Alternative: switch the expression to `Math.mulDiv` and bound the result at a documented safe ceiling.
severityRationale: CONFIRM low. Defensive hardening recommendation. Documented parameter envelope keeps the product well below 2^256; the suggested mulDiv / explicit overflow-precheck makes the contract robust to future configuration changes. Solvency invariant preserved via emergencyWithdraw escape hatch. QA report.

scannerAttribution.dedupNotes: No econ-scanner counterpart (econ-scanner instead verified M-03 fix robustness from the participation-multiplier angle and explicitly concluded ROBUST). The overflow concern is orthogonal to participation correctness — kept as the only mechanical hardening item on the NFTStaker M-03 code path.

sanitization.notes: Not in any prior submission (M-03 in phoenix-nft-staking-05 dealt with the rate-sizing basis change, not the multiplicative overflow envelope). Not in known issues. The known-issue 'M-03 staked-subset sizing' is the FIX whose internals this finding examines for overflow safety; flagging an arithmetic-envelope hardening on the resulting expression is orthogonal and legitimate.
